To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

We have demonstrated the successful three-dimensional growth of smooth muscle cells and stem cells in a hydrogel matrix, and have demonstrated differentiation of smooth muscle cells into a contractile, quiescent phenotype, and of stem cells into functional smooth muscle.

the use of hydrogel scaffolds for 3-dimensional cell culture is a promising approach to study bladder smooth muscle cell differentiation, and that this approach may contribute to the understanding underlying basic mechanisms of smooth muscle cell differentiation.
we have developed an innovative method to culture bladder smooth muscle cells and mesenchymmal stem cells in a 3D hydrogel matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the reconstruction of the human bladder.
the development of an adequate temporary scaffold, which allows cell attachment and proliferation while synthesis of extra cellular matrix proteins and tissue organisation take place.
the development of new methods for the regeneration of bladder tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydrogel matrix provides an adequate environment for smooth muscle cells and mesenchyma stem cells to differentiate and proliferate.
the hydrogel system is an excellent tool for studying the differentiation of human bladder smooth muscles and mesenchymale stem cells.
the presented model can be used for studying the mechanisms of smooth muscle cell differentiation as a basis for bladder tissue engineering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new 3-D culture system for human bladder smooth muscle and stem cells.
the hydrogel system is an adequate temporary scaffold for cell attachment and proliferation, allowing the cells to synthesize extra-cellular matrix components.
we have developed a model that can be used to investigate the mechanisms of bladder tissue engineering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of hydrogels for tissue engineering of the bladder may lead to a more successful reconstruction of the bladder.
we can now grow human smooth muscle cells and mesenchymale stem cells three-dimensionally.
we can now study the effects of drugs, growth factors, and mechanical stimuli on bladder smooth muscle cells and mesenchymmal stem cells in a more physiological setting.
